chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Sam'ah, from Aban, from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the grandfather, if he marries off his son's daughter, and her father is alive, and the grandfather is acceptable (approved), it is valid. We said: 'But if the father of the girl has a preference and the grandfather has a preference, and they are equal in justice and approval,' he said: 'I prefer that she accept the word of the grandfather.'
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to arrange marriage if both the father and paternal grandfather are alive and equally qualified?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the hierarchy of marriage guardianship (wilayah) is clarified, establishing that the paternal grandfather holds precedence over the father when both are alive and equally qualified. The Imam’s preference for the grandfather’s choice in cases of equal standing reflects the scholarly view that the grandfather, being closer in lineage and often possessing greater authority, acts as the primary guardian in the absence of the father's explicit disqualification. This ruling underscores the importance of familial hierarchy in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the most senior eligible male relative guides the marriage contract to preserve family honor and compatibility.
